documents: Koenig et al. 2022, JGR Oceans 127, e2021JC018357, published paper (PDF, 13 pages)

entry.evidence: In July and September 2017, we deployed a glider west and north of Svalbard to investigate the AW properties and pathways in this region

steps.action: Frame the question of how Atlantic Water is transformed and routed through its branches north and west of Svalbard, drawing on the literature.
steps.quote: Some of the key locations for water mass transformation of the AW are west and north of Svalbard

steps.action: Take from the authors' July-August 2017 glider mission the idea that shelf-origin cold, fresh lenses cool the WSC core and that their presence depends on the wind regime.
steps.quote: The presence of these lenses from the shelf can be related to the wind regime.

steps.action: Take from Nilsen et al. (2021) the relation between wind stress curl and volume transport anomalies across the Yermak Plateau.
steps.quote: demonstrate a significant correlation between the wind stress curl over the northeastern Fram Strait and volume transport anomaly across the YP

steps.action: Fly a SeaExplorer glider (CTD, oxygen, chlorophyll, CDOM, backscatter) from the WSC across the Yermak Plateau to the Sofia Deep; correct thermal lag, grid to 1 m, and compute detided depth-averaged currents from dead reckoning.
steps.quote: The glider sampled the ocean along a sawtooth trajectory from the surface down to a maximum depth of 700 m

steps.action: Compare glider CTD data with the nearest ship CTD casts to estimate glider temperature and salinity accuracy (result not shown).
steps.quote: A comparison between glider and ship CTD data resulted in an estimated glider accuracy of

steps.action: Collect a 13-station ship CTD/LADCP section above the southern Yermak Plateau, crossing the glider track.
steps.quote: 13 CTD stations were performed on 24 September 2017 along a section above the southern YP

steps.action: Characterize the wind conditions from ERA5 for 2010-2020 and find that summer 2017 had anomalous southerly winds; add Nora3 winds for detail.
steps.quote: The southerly winds observed in summer 2017 deviate from the average for the past decade north of Svalbard

steps.action: Describe the water masses and currents in seven zones along the glider track, including two shelf-origin cold, fresh, CDOM-rich lenses in the WSC and the YB, YPB, and Sofia Deep properties.
steps.quote: These lenses originate from the shelf

steps.action: Compare zone 1 properties with the WSC sampled in July 2017 and find them comparable.
steps.quote: Zone 1 hydrographic properties are comparable to those sampled in the WSC in July 2017

steps.action: Compare LADCP along-slope velocities with the expected Svalbard Branch at the 400 m isobath and find no significant eastward flow there; flag the coarse station spacing.
steps.quote: There is no significant eastward velocities above the 400 m isobath as would be expected with the SB

steps.action: Map the 0-300 m averaged temperature and salinity along the glider and CTD tracks to show AW transformation from the western to the eastern YP.
steps.quote: The averaged temperature and salinity in the upper 300 m illustrate the AW mass transformation and pathways over the YP.

steps.action: Check the glider-CTD intersection: below 50 m the averages agree, and the authors attribute the surface difference to northward advection of meltwater over five days.
steps.quote: The temperature and salinity averages below 50 m (50–300 m) at the two dates are comparable

steps.action: Compute Nora3 wind stress curl over the CTD section and find a strongly positive event on 19-20 September tied to southerly winds.
steps.quote: Wind stress curl estimated from the high-resolution model (Nora3) in the area of the CTD section was strongly positive during 19–20 September

steps.action: Retain the claim that the detached lenses settle at their density level below the AW core and so cool and freshen the AW from below.
steps.quote: Hence, the lenses described here cool and freshen the AW core from below.

steps.action: Propose that lens detachment follows southerly wind bursts and their relaxation, via onshore Ekman transport and mixing on the shelf (after Koenig et al. 2018 and Nilsen et al. 2016).
steps.quote: can be a consequence of the southerly wind bursts and their subsequent relaxation

steps.action: Cite the Kolås and Fer (2018) rival mechanism (convectively driven bottom mixing and downslope Ekman transport) and judge it compatible, not excluded.
steps.quote: The two processes described above do not exclude each other.

steps.action: Speculate that the paired westward and eastward flows at the shelf break mark a roughly 4 km eddy; the CTD resolution leaves this unconfirmed.
steps.quote: We could speculate that it was the signature of an eddy with a radius of about 4 km

steps.action: Take from Nilsen et al. (2021) the expectation that positive wind stress curl weakens the SB through surface divergence and a 12-15 hr geostrophic adjustment.
steps.quote: As suggested by Nilsen et al. (2021), the variability in the SB is controlled by the wind stress curl on the shelf.

steps.action: Compare the 19-20 September wind stress curl magnitude with the events in Nilsen et al. (2021) and find it of similar order.
steps.quote: which is of similar order of magnitude as the wind events discussed in Nilsen [...] )

steps.action: Retain the anomalous southerly winds and the positive curl event as the explanation for the weak SB at its usual 400 m isobath on 24 September.
steps.quote: The strongly anomalous southerly wind conditions and associated adjustments of ocean isopycnals can explain why the SB was weak

steps.action: Set the observed weak SB against operational-model studies (Koenig et al. 2017; Athanase et al. 2021) that also show a weak SB in September 2017.
steps.quote: has shown a particularly weak SB at the shelf break in September 2017

end.claim: In September 2017 the Svalbard Branch was weak at its usual 400 m isobath, explained by anomalous southerly winds and a positive wind stress curl event, while detached shelf-water lenses cooled and freshened the AW inflow from below.

decisive_move.sentence: The glider crossing of the Yermak Plateau, together with the ship CTD/LADCP section, supplied the lens observations and the missing SB flow at the 400 m isobath on which both claims rest.

gates.evidence: The September mission was deployed to document AW properties and pathways (p. 2), not to test a stated hypothesis. The wind explanations for the lenses and the weak SB were invoked after the observations from cited mechanisms (Nilsen et al. 2016, 2021), with no test that could have failed (pp. 10-11). Nothing was fixed in advance.

imports.item: dead-reckoning navigation with GPS surface fixes to derive depth-averaged currents

limits: Coded from the published PDF only; there was no review file, so no review sequence. Several supporting checks are reported as 'not shown': the glider vs ship CTD accuracy, the maximum tidal amplitude, and the 50-300 m agreement at the intersection. The wind-forcing explanation for the weak SB and for lens detachment was not tested: no model run, no counterfactual, and no comparison with non-southerly periods (inference). The SB claim rests on a coarse CTD section (2-10 km spacing) that the authors themselves flag. The eddy interpretation is left unconfirmed. Sub-claims and their statuses: the lenses cool and freshen the AW from below is best_explanation, based on density level alone, and the authors say quantification needs further investigation (p. 11); the expectation that such circulation will become more frequent (p. 12) is an extrapolation with no status. Composition is none_fits: this is a single-campaign observational case study in which conditions were found in a live event and a mechanism was taken from the literature, with neither repeated independent traces (trace_series) nor a crucial test. The choice of Nora3 over ERA5 is justified by resolution, but its effect is not reported.

disagreements.target: Literature position that the Svalbard Branch follows the 400 m isobath (Cokelet et al. 2008 and others)
disagreements.support: LADCP velocities on 24 September 2017 show no significant eastward flow at the 400 m isobath, which the authors attribute to wind forcing.
disagreements.quote: There is no significant eastward velocities above the 400 m isobath as would be expected with the SB

disagreements.target: Kolås and Fer (2018) lens origin by convectively driven bottom mixing
disagreements.support: The authors propose a wind-driven detachment mechanism and state that it is compatible with, not opposed to, the Kolås and Fer mechanism.
disagreements.quote: The two processes described above do not exclude each other.

alternatives_considered.chosen: Wind-burst-and-relaxation detachment of shelf lenses (after Koenig et al. 2018; Nilsen et al. 2016)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Convectively driven bottom mixing and downslope Ekman transport (Kolås & Fer 2018)
alternatives_considered.reason: The two processes do not exclude each other

alternatives_considered.chosen: Nora3 3 km hindcast winds for the September 2017 detail
alternatives_considered.reason: Higher spatial resolution and more accurate wind reanalysis north of Svalbard (Haakenstad et al. 2021)

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Signature of an eddy with a radius of about 4 km
alternatives_considered.reason: The spatial resolution of the CTD data prevents confirmation
